procedure_steps.detail: Find the relevant CREA-MEDIA call on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
Register your company and obtain a PIC.
Submit the single-stage proposal by the deadline. Contact your national Creative Europe Desk for guidance.

Company track record / previous works evidence

programmes.name_en: Digital Europe Programme
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG CNECT), implemented by HaDEA and EISMEA
programmes.amount_note: Programme budget is 'over €8.1 billion' for the Multiannual Financial Framework 2021-2027. Grant sizes and co-funding rates are set per topic in the annual work programmes (typically 50% for most actions and higher for some, but this was not stated on the official programme page, so cofunding_pct is null here rather than guessed).
programmes.deadline_note: Calls published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal under the DIGITAL programme, with topic-specific deadlines set in the annual work programmes.

procedure_steps.detail: Search the DIGITAL programme page on the Funding & Tenders Portal for open topics.
Register your organisation and obtain a PIC.
Submit the proposal by the topic deadline. Many DIGITAL topics fund consortia or European Digital Innovation Hubs, which then deliver free or subsidised services to SMEs.

documents_required.doc: Proposal Part A and Part B
PIC for every partner

eligibility.other_note: The programme 'supports industry, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and public administration in their digital transformation'. Thematic areas: 'supercomputing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced digital skills, and ensuring a wide use of digital technologies across the economy and society', plus semiconductors added in September 2023. Important nuance for aggregators: much of the SME-facing value flows indirectly, via European Digital Innovation Hubs, whose services to an SME may themselves count as de minimis aid at national level.

programmes.source_snippet: With an overall budget of over €8.1 billion, DIGITAL aims to shape the digital transformation ... supercomputing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced digital skills, and ensuring a wide use of digital technologies across the economy and society

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Accelerator
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) / European Commission, under Horizon Europe
programmes.amount_note: Grant component is a lump sum contribution 'below EUR 2.5 million' for innovation activities (TRL 6-8), to be completed within 24 months. A separate investment component of EUR 1-10 million in direct equity or quasi-equity is available via the EIC Fund (blended finance), or investment-only. Because the grant is a lump sum, there is no published percentage funding rate. 2026 budgets: EUR 414 million for Accelerator Open, EUR 220 million for Accelerator Challenges.
programmes.deadline_note: Step 1 short proposals may be submitted at any time and are batched every first Tuesday of the month at 17:00 Brussels time. Step 2 full proposals are batched at 17:00 Brussels time on 07/01/2026, 04/03/2026, 06/05/2026, 08/07/2026, 02/09/2026 and 04/11/2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Write your short proposal: a 12-page form, a pitch deck of up to ten slides in PDF, and a video pitch of up to three minutes. Evaluated remotely by 4 EIC expert evaluators; feedback normally in 4-6 weeks.

If the short proposal receives a GO, prepare the full proposal on the Funding and Tenders portal: a 20-page form, pitch deck, implementation plan, financial information, Letters of Intent, freedom-to-operate analysis and a 3-minute video pitch. Results within 8-9 weeks.
Pitch your innovation face-to-face to the EIC Jury (top-ranked proposals corresponding to 2.5 times the available grant budget are invited). Interview results within 2-3 weeks.
Sign the Grant Agreement and receive first pre-financing. For blended finance, the case is transmitted to the EIC Fund and the investment need is assessed; investment decided within 2-6 months.

documents_required.doc: Short proposal form (12 pages)
Pitch deck (up to 10 slides, PDF)
Video pitch (up to 3 minutes, core team of up to 3 people)
Full proposal form (20 pages)
Implementation plan and financial information
Letters of Intent
Freedom-to-operate (FTO) analysis
PIC (Participant Identification Code) from the EU Funding & Tenders Portal

eligibility.other_note: Single start-up or SME (including spin-outs); small mid-caps up to 499 employees may apply for the investment component only; natural persons or legal entities willing to set up an SME or mid-cap may also apply. Applicants from third countries may relocate their company before Step 2 to become eligible. UK applicants can only apply for the 'grant only' scheme. Only one application at a time. Grant-only support may be provided only once during Horizon Europe 2021-2027. Horizon Europe grants are not de minimis aid; they are direct EU management funds, so the Regulation (EU) 2023/2831 ceiling does not apply.

programmes.source_snippet: Grant component below EUR 2.5 million. Up to € 10 million of equity investments, coaching & mentoring, networking. ... Single start-up or SME (including spin-outs); Small mid-caps (up to 499 employees) in need of rapid scale up of the TRL 9 activity. Mid-caps can apply for investment only.

Register on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and obtain a PIC.

programmes.source_snippet: Single Applicants: Permitted for Pathfinder Challenges only ... Pathfinder Challenges: 28 October 2026

Funding rates follow Horizon Europe rules (100% for RIA, 70% for for-profit participants in Innovation Actions). Some JUs additionally require private members to match with in-kind contributions.
programmes.deadline_note: One or two calls per year published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, usually opening in Q1 or Q2 with deadlines a few months later.
programmes.reopen_note: Each Joint Undertaking publishes an annual work programme setting the next call dates; check the JU website for the current calendar.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium requirements as in Horizon Europe. SMEs and start-ups participate as consortium partners; some JUs give SMEs a higher funding rate or reserved budget. Membership of the JU's private association is not required to apply but is common among coordinators.

programmes.name_en: Creative Europe Cross-sectoral strand (incl. Innovation Lab, Journalism Partnerships)
programmes.amount_note: Covers the Creative Innovation Lab (cross-sector innovation between audiovisual, culture and other sectors), Journalism Partnerships and News Media support. Co-funding is typically up to 70-80% of eligible costs; budgets are set per call.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual calls; the Creative Innovation Lab has typically had a spring deadline.
programmes.reopen_note: Re-issued each year under the annual Creative Europe work programme.

eligibility.other_note: Consortia of organisations from Creative Europe countries; creative-tech SMEs are eligible partners and are explicitly targeted by the Innovation Lab.

programmes.name_en: Creative Europe Culture strand
programmes.amount_note: European Cooperation Projects are funded at up to 80% of eligible costs, with three categories: small-scale (up to EUR 200,000), medium-scale (up to EUR 1 million) and large-scale (up to EUR 2 million). Separate schemes cover literary translation, networks and platforms, and mobility (Culture Moves Europe).
programmes.deadline_note: European Cooperation Projects has one annual deadline, historically in January. Other schemes have their own dates.
programmes.reopen_note: Annual cycle; the European Cooperation Projects call has consistently opened in autumn with a January deadline.

eligibility.other_note: Cultural and creative organisations (including creative SMEs) legally established in a Creative Europe country. Small-scale projects need at least 3 partners from 3 countries; larger categories need more.

programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA strand
programmes.amount_note: Multiple schemes with different ceilings: development of single projects and slates, TV and online content, video game and immersive content development, European co-production funds, distribution, innovative tools and business models, and MEDIA 360. Grants are typically lump sums; single project development grants have been in the EUR 25,000-60,000 range and slate funding higher.
programmes.deadline_note: Each MEDIA scheme has its own annual deadline; the calendar is published in the annual Creative Europe work programme, with deadlines spread across the year.
programmes.reopen_note: MEDIA schemes are re-issued annually. Check the EACEA Funding & Tenders pages for each scheme's current deadline.

eligibility.other_note: Independent European audiovisual production, distribution, video game and immersive content companies established in a Creative Europe country. Most schemes require a track record of previously produced or distributed works.

programmes.name_local: Creative Europe MEDIA - Innovative Tools and Business Models
programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA Innovative Tools and Business Models
programmes.amount_note: Grants for technology and business model innovation across the audiovisual value chain, covering up to 70% of eligible costs. Project budgets commonly run to several hundred thousand euro.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual call with a fixed deadline published on the Funding & Tenders Portal.

eligibility.other_note: Companies established in a Creative Europe participating country; consortium applications are common but single applicants are eligible for some topics.

programmes.name_local: Creative Europe MEDIA - European Slate Development
programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA European Slate Development support
programmes.amount_note: Lump sum support for the development of a slate of three to five audiovisual projects, historically in the range of EUR 60,000 to EUR 300,000 per slate at up to 50% of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual call, historically with a deadline in the autumn or early in the year.

eligibility.other_note: Independent European audiovisual production companies with a recent track record; established in a Creative Europe participating country.

programmes.name_local: Creative Europe MEDIA - European Video Games and Immersive Content Development
programmes.name_en: Creative Europe MEDIA video games and immersive content development support
programmes.funder: European Commission / European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA)
programmes.amount_note: Lump sum grants for the development phase of video games, XR and immersive projects. Historically EUR 10,000 to EUR 300,000 per project depending on the total development budget, capped at 50% of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: One call per year with a fixed deadline, historically in the first quarter.

eligibility.other_note: European production companies established in a Creative Europe participating country, majority-owned by nationals of participating countries, with a track record of a previously released work.

programmes.source_snippet: The MEDIA strand of the Creative Europe programme supports the European film and audiovisual industries to develop, distribute and promote European works, taking into account today's digital environment.

programmes.name_en: Digital Europe Programme (DIGITAL)
programmes.amount_note: Deployment programme (not research). Co-funding rate is normally 50% of eligible costs for grants, rising to 75% for SMEs in some topics and 100% for certain coordination actions. Project budgets typically range from EUR 1 million to tens of millions.
programmes.deadline_note: Calls are launched under the biennial DIGITAL Work Programme, usually with one to three deadline waves per year across AI, cybersecurity, advanced digital skills, data spaces, semiconductors and deployment of digital capacities.

eligibility.other_note: Open to legal entities in EU Member States and DIGITAL-associated countries. Some topics (cybersecurity, semiconductors) are restricted to EU-controlled entities. Consortium requirements vary by topic.

programmes.name_local: ESF+ EaSI strand - social economy and social innovation
programmes.name_en: EU ESF+ Employment and Social Innovation (EaSI) strand
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG EMPL) via EISMEA and the EU Programme for Employment and Social Innovation
programmes.amount_note: Calls supporting social economy ecosystems, social enterprise finance and social innovation. Grants normally cover up to 80-90% of eligible costs; project sizes commonly range from a few hundred thousand to a few million euro.
programmes.deadline_note: EaSI calls are published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal with fixed deadlines, typically a handful per year.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are usually public bodies, social economy networks or intermediaries rather than individual social enterprises; social enterprises benefit as end recipients. The InvestEU Social Investment and Skills window provides complementary guarantees to lenders.

programmes.name_en: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) services for SMEs
programmes.funder: European Commission (Digital Europe Programme) and national co-funding
programmes.amount_note: No cash to the SME. EDIHs provide 'test before invest' services, AI/HPC/cybersecurity experimentation, digital skills training and innovation-ecosystem access, delivered free or heavily subsidised under de minimis rules. Value per SME is capped by state-aid rules rather than a published grant amount.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous. SMEs approach their nearest EDIH directly; each hub has its own intake process.

eligibility.other_note: SMEs and public sector organisations located in the EDIH's region. Services are subsidised under de minimis state aid, so prior de minimis aid received counts against the ceiling.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Accelerator
programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 2.5 million grant for technology development and market readiness, combined with an optional EIC Fund equity investment (typically EUR 0.5-10 million, and up to EUR 15 million in some cases) through 'blended finance'.
programmes.deadline_note: Short applications can be submitted at any time; full proposals have fixed cut-offs. 2026 full-proposal cut-offs: 7 January, 4 March, 6 May, 8 July, 2 September and 4 November 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the short application (pitch deck, video and form) at any time via the EIC AI platform
If successful, submit a full proposal before one of the published cut-offs
Face-to-face (or remote) jury interview for shortlisted companies
Grant agreement preparation and, for blended finance, EIC Fund due diligence

documents_required.doc: Short application form
Pitch deck
Video pitch
Full business plan (Annex)
Company financials

eligibility.other_note: Single SMEs (including startups and small mid-caps for the investment component) established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country. Technology must be at TRL 5-8 for the grant.

programmes.source_snippet: EIC Accelerator: Scale-Up Grants & Investments for scaling up business. Deadlines: 7.01.2026 | 4.03.2026 | 6.05.2026 | 8.07.2026 | 2.09.2026 | 4.11.2026

programmes.name_en: EIC Accelerator Challenges (thematic calls)
programmes.amount_note: Same instrument as EIC Accelerator Open (grant up to EUR 2.5m lump sum, optional EUR 1-10m equity) but restricted to named strategic technology Challenges. 2026 budget for Challenges EUR 220 million.
programmes.deadline_note: EIC Accelerator 2026 short-proposal cut-offs at 17:00 Brussels time: 7 Jan, 4 Mar, 6 May, 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026. Challenge topics are fixed for the year and change annually.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the Challenge topics published in the annual EIC Work Programme
Submit short proposal selecting the relevant Challenge
Full proposal at a Challenge-specific cut-off
EIC Jury interview
Grant agreement / investment due diligence

eligibility.other_note: Proposal must fall inside a named Challenge for that year's work programme. Same SME/small mid-cap eligibility as the Open track.

programmes.source_snippet: EUR 220 million to Accelerator Challenges and EUR 414 million to the Accelerator Open track

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Accelerator (Open)
programmes.amount_note: Grant-only component is a lump sum below EUR 2.5 million for innovation activities over max 24 months. Can be combined with an EIC Fund equity investment of EUR 1-10 million (blended finance). 2026 Open track budget EUR 414 million.
programmes.deadline_note: EIC Accelerator 2026 short-proposal cut-offs at 17:00 Brussels time: 7 Jan, 4 Mar, 6 May, 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit a short proposal any time (12-page form, pitch deck, 3-minute video) via the EIC AI-assisted platform
Await evaluation result; short proposals are batched at each cut-off
If successful, submit the full proposal (up to 20 pages plus annexes) at a chosen full-proposal cut-off
If successful, attend the EIC Jury face-to-face/remote interview
Grant agreement preparation; for blended finance, EIC Fund investment due diligence runs in parallel

documents_required.doc: Short proposal form (business idea, team, market)
Pitch deck
3-minute video pitch by the core team
Full proposal (business plan, freedom-to-operate, financials)
Proof of SME status / company registration
Declaration of ownership and control

eligibility.other_note: Single SME (incl. spin-outs, start-ups) or small mid-cap (up to 499 employees) established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country. Individuals planning to create a company are also eligible. TRL 5-8 at entry.

programmes.source_snippet: Lump sum contribution below EUR 2.5 million ... equity or quasi-equity investments EUR 1 - EUR 10 million

programmes.name_en: EIC Business Acceleration Services (BAS)
programmes.amount_note: No cash. Free coaching, mentoring, investor matchmaking, corporate partnering days, access to the EIC Community platform and to services such as the EIC Women Leadership Programme. Delivered to EIC beneficiaries and, for some services, to the wider EIC Community.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous; services are requested through the EIC Community platform.

eligibility.other_note: Primarily for EIC-funded companies (Accelerator, Transition, Pathfinder) and EIC Prize winners; some open services for the wider EIC Community.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Fund (direct equity)
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council Fund (managed by EIF/Alter Domus on behalf of the European Commission)
programmes.amount_note: Direct equity/quasi-equity. Standard EIC Accelerator blended-finance ticket is EUR 1-10 million. Under the STEP Scale-Up strand tickets of up to EUR 30 million are possible. The EIC Fund typically takes a 10-20% minority stake and does not seek control.
programmes.deadline_note: No separate application: companies access the EIC Fund by being selected through the EIC Accelerator or the EIC Scale-Up strand.

eligibility.other_note: Only companies selected via EIC Accelerator / EIC Scale-Up. Investment is subject to due diligence and to EU ownership and control screening.

programmes.name_en: European Innovation Council Pathfinder
programmes.amount_note: Research and innovation grants for breakthrough research from laboratory to prototype. Pathfinder Open awards are typically up to EUR 3 million; Pathfinder Challenges up to EUR 4 million. Funding is at 100% of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Pathfinder Open normally has one cut-off per year (historically in spring) and Pathfinder Challenges one in the autumn. Check the EIC funding opportunities page for the current dates.

eligibility.other_note: Pathfinder Open requires a consortium of at least three partners from three countries; single applicants (including startups and research organisations) are allowed in some configurations. TRL 1-4.

programmes.source_snippet: EIC Pathfinder: Research & Innovation grants for breakthrough research from laboratory to prototype

programmes.name_en: EIC Pathfinder Challenges
programmes.amount_note: Indicative EUR 3-4 million per project depending on the Challenge; 100% of eligible costs. Challenge topics are set annually in the EIC Work Programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Single annual cut-off, historically in October.
programmes.reopen_note: Runs annually; the Challenge portfolio is renewed with each EIC Work Programme (adopted around Q4 for the following year).

eligibility.other_note: Consortium of at least 3 independent entities from 3 different eligible countries, or a single legal entity where the Challenge allows it.

programmes.name_en: EIC Pathfinder Open
programmes.amount_note: Indicative EUR 3 million per project for consortia doing early-stage, high-risk technology research (TRL 1-4). Larger amounts possible if justified. 100% funding of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: One annual cut-off, historically in spring (Pathfinder Open) with results in autumn.
programmes.reopen_note: Pathfinder Open runs as a single annual call under each EIC Work Programme; the next call is published with the following year's EIC Work Programme, typically adopted in Q4.

procedure_steps.detail: Read the EIC Work Programme Pathfinder section
Form a consortium of at least 3 independent legal entities from 3 different countries (or apply as a single entity for Pathfinder Open)
Submit the full proposal on the EU Funding & Tenders portal by the annual deadline
Remote expert evaluation
Grant agreement preparation

eligibility.other_note: Open to consortia and to single legal entities (SMEs incl. start-ups, spin-offs, research organisations, universities). Focus on TRL 1-4 science-to-technology breakthroughs.

programmes.name_en: EIC Pre-Accelerator for widening countries
programmes.amount_note: Support for technology and business development aimed at companies in Horizon Europe widening countries preparing for the EIC Accelerator. Grant size is set in the call text.
programmes.deadline_note: Listed among EIC funding opportunities; check the EIC page for the current call window.

eligibility.other_note: Targets startups and SMEs established in Horizon Europe widening countries (mostly central, eastern and southern Europe plus associated countries).

programmes.source_snippet: EIC Pre-Accelerator: Targets technology and business development in widening countries

programmes.name_en: EIC Prizes (incl. European Innovation Procurement Awards)
programmes.amount_note: Inducement and recognition prizes; individual prize amounts are set per contest in the EIC Work Programme and have historically ranged from tens of thousands to several million euro. No co-funding required; the prize is paid on award.
programmes.deadline_note: Prize contests are launched individually, each with its own deadline, announced in the annual EIC Work Programme.
programmes.reopen_note: New prize contests are announced with each EIC Work Programme; check the EIC prizes page for currently open contests.

eligibility.other_note: Eligibility is contest-specific; most EIC prizes are open to legal entities established in the EU or a Horizon Europe associated country.

programmes.name_en: EIC STEP Scale-Up
programmes.funder: European Innovation Council Fund / European Commission
programmes.amount_note: Equity-only instrument for later-stage European deep-tech companies raising large rounds; tickets reported at EUR 10-30 million, always alongside private co-investors. No grant component.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling submission with periodic assessment; introduced under the STEP (Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform) framework in the EIC Work Programme.

eligibility.other_note: Targets scale-ups in STEP strategic technology areas (deep tech and digital, clean and resource-efficient tech, biotech). Requires committed private co-investment.

programmes.name_en: EIC STEP Scale Up equity investment
programmes.amount_note: Equity investments intended to catalyse larger investment rounds of EUR 50 million or above, helping European deep tech companies become global leaders.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 cut-offs: 11 February, 6 May, 9 September and 25 November 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Aimed at companies raising rounds of EUR 50 million or above in STEP priority areas (deep and digital technologies, clean technologies, biotechnologies).

programmes.source_snippet: Equity investments to catalyse larger investments rounds of €50 million or above. Deadlines: 11.02.2026 | 6.05.2026 | 9.09.2026 | 25.11.2026

programmes.name_en: EIC STEP Scale Up Defence
programmes.amount_note: Dedicated strand of STEP Scale Up supporting strategic defence and dual-use technologies. Investment sizes follow the STEP Scale Up model.
programmes.deadline_note: Follows the STEP Scale Up cut-off calendar; check the EIC funding opportunities page for the defence-specific dates.

eligibility.other_note: Supports strategic defence technologies developed by EU-established companies.

programmes.source_snippet: EIC STEP Scale Up Defence: A specialized program supporting strategic defense technologies

programmes.name_en: EIC Transition
programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 2.5 million per project (higher amounts possible if justified), 100% of eligible costs, to mature a technology from TRL 4 to TRL 5-6 and build the business case.
programmes.deadline_note: Single annual cut-off, historically in September/October.
programmes.reopen_note: EIC Transition has run as an annual single-cut-off call; the next deadline is set in the EIC Work Programme for the coming year.

procedure_steps.detail: Verify that your technology originates from an eligible prior project (EIC Pathfinder, FET, ERC Proof of Concept, EDF, national/regional programme as listed in the Work Programme)
Prepare a full proposal covering technology maturation and business readiness
Submit on the EU Funding & Tenders portal
Remote evaluation and interview for shortlisted proposals
Grant agreement

eligibility.other_note: Results must build on eligible prior EU or national research results. Single SME/spin-off or small consortium (2-5 partners).

programmes.name_en: Horizon Europe European Innovation Ecosystems, CONNECT strand
programmes.amount_note: Coordination and Support Actions plus Innovation Actions connecting regional innovation ecosystems. Project budgets typically EUR 1-6 million per topic. Several CONNECT projects run cascade funding (financial support to third parties) that re-grants to start-ups, commonly in the EUR 10,000-60,000 range per company.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual calls under the EIE work programme. The 2026 call (HORIZON-EIE-2026-01) includes topics such as Expanding Investment Ecosystems (CONNECT-02) and Scaling up deep tech ecosystems (CONNECT-03).

eligibility.other_note: Direct applicants are typically consortia of ecosystem actors (clusters, agencies, incubators, universities). Start-ups usually benefit via the funded projects' cascade calls.

programmes.source_snippet: Scaling up deep tech ecosystems (HORIZON-EIE-2026-01-CONNECT-03)

programmes.name_en: Horizon Europe European Innovation Ecosystems, SCALEUP strand
programmes.amount_note: Supports the scale-up of innovation ecosystems and instruments such as Women TechEU and innovation procurement support. Budgets per topic are published in the EIE work programme; many actions include financial support to third parties passed on to start-ups.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual EIE calls; SCALEUP topics appear alongside CONNECT topics in the same work programme.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium-based. Deep-tech scale-ups can be direct partners in some topics and cascade beneficiaries in others.

programmes.name_local: EIF equity investments in VC and business angel funds
programmes.name_en: European Investment Fund equity mandates (InvestEU, ESCALAR, EIC Fund fund-of-funds)
programmes.amount_note: The EIF invests as a limited partner in venture capital funds, business angel co-investment vehicles and technology transfer funds rather than in start-ups directly. Founders benefit indirectly: a large share of European seed and Series A funds are EIF-backed. Ticket sizes into funds run from single-digit to hundreds of millions of euro.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous, via published calls for expression of interest addressed to fund managers.

eligibility.other_note: Direct applicants must be fund managers or financial intermediaries, not start-ups. Start-ups receive EIF money through the funds it backs.

programmes.name_en: EIT Climate-KIC Climate Entrepreneurship / Accelerator
programmes.amount_note: EIT Climate-KIC has historically run a staged accelerator paying equity-free grants per stage (commonly EUR 15,000 at Stage 1, EUR 25,000 Stage 2, EUR 50,000 Stage 3) plus coaching. The flagship pan-European Accelerator has been restructured into regional and challenge-led entrepreneurship programmes; check current offers.
programmes.deadline_note: The classic three-stage EIT Climate-KIC Accelerator is no longer offered as a single pan-European call; entrepreneurship support now runs through regional hubs, ClimAccelerator-branded programmes and challenge calls with their own deadlines.
programmes.reopen_note: ClimAccelerator programmes are launched by regional partners at different times of year; browse climate-kic.org opportunities for the currently open ones.

eligibility.other_note: Climate-impact start-ups; specific eligibility set by each regional ClimAccelerator.

programmes.name_en: EIT Climate-KIC ClimAccelerator
programmes.amount_note: Delivered as a network of thematic and geographic ClimAccelerator programmes run by local partners. Equity-free grants have historically ranged in the low tens of thousands of euro per venture, but each local accelerator sets its own terms.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual ClimAccelerator programmes open their own calls, mostly in the first half of the year. EIT Climate-KIC restructured its entrepreneurship offering; check the organisation's open calls page for the currently running accelerators.

eligibility.other_note: Programmes are typically restricted to teams based in the EU Member State or region hosting the individual ClimAccelerator.

programmes.source_snippet: Climate entrepreneurship is listed among EIT Climate-KIC focus areas; specific accelerator calls are published under the organisation's open calls section.

programmes.name_en: EIT Culture & Creativity start-up support
programmes.amount_note: Newest KIC (launched 2023). Runs acceleration, incubation and challenge calls for cultural and creative sector ventures across five regional co-location centres. Grant amounts are set per call; several calls have offered five-figure equity-free grants.
programmes.deadline_note: Multiple calls per year across regional co-location centres; each has its own deadline.
programmes.reopen_note: EIT Culture & Creativity publishes an annual business creation call portfolio; check the opportunities page for the current window.

eligibility.other_note: Ventures in cultural and creative sectors and industries (architecture, design, fashion, audiovisual, gaming, heritage, music) in EU/associated countries.

programmes.name_en: EIT Digital Venture Programme / Venture Incubation
programmes.funder: EIT Digital (European Institute of Innovation and Technology)
programmes.amount_note: EIT Digital supports deep-tech digital ventures with an incubation/acceleration package. Cash support amounts are set per call and per venture; EIT Digital has historically combined non-dilutive support with an option to invest. Confirm the current package on the call page.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual open call for ventures, usually with an autumn/winter deadline.
programmes.reopen_note: EIT Digital publishes venture calls annually; monitor eitdigital.eu for the next window.

eligibility.other_note: Digital deep-tech ventures based in the EU or a Horizon Europe associated country.

programmes.name_en: EIT Food Accelerator Network (FAN)
programmes.amount_note: Equity-free acceleration programme run in several European city hubs. Participants receive a grant/stipend towards programme participation and travel plus access to corporate pilots; EIT Food does not take equity. Cash amounts are set per edition.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual cohort. Applications have typically opened around December-February for a programme starting mid-year.
programmes.reopen_note: FAN has run annually since 2018 across hubs including Bilbao, Munich, Warsaw, Haifa and Milan; the next call is announced on eitfood.eu in winter.

eligibility.other_note: Agrifood-tech start-ups with a working prototype or early revenue. Company must be able to participate in the on-site hub programme.

programmes.name_en: EIT Food Seedbed Incubator
programmes.amount_note: Pre-incubation programme for researchers and very early founders. Participants receive a travel/validation stipend and a market-validation curriculum; equity-free. Stipend amounts set per edition.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual intake, usually with applications closing in the first months of the year.
programmes.reopen_note: Seedbed runs annually; announcements appear on eitfood.eu early in the calendar year.

eligibility.other_note: Open to researchers, PhD students and pre-incorporation teams with an agrifood idea, as well as very early-stage companies.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Catapult
programmes.amount_note: Competition-style accelerator across Biotech, Medtech and Digital Health tracks. Winners receive cash prizes (historically EUR 20,000-50,000 per track winner) plus intensive coaching and investor exposure. Exact prize amounts vary by edition.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual competition; applications typically open in spring with semi-finals in autumn and finals at the EIT Health Summit.
programmes.reopen_note: Catapult runs annually; the next application window is announced on eithealth.eu, usually in spring.

eligibility.other_note: Early-stage health innovators in Biotech, Medtech or Digital Health from EU/associated countries.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Headstart
programmes.amount_note: Equity-free grant of up to EUR 75,000 per start-up to reach a defined commercial milestone (regulatory, clinical validation, market entry). Awarded through regional EIT Health InnoStars/CLC calls.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual call run through EIT Health regional offices (CLCs and InnoStars), typically opening in Q1 with a spring deadline.
programmes.reopen_note: Headstart has run every year since 2018 with a Q1-Q2 application window through the regional EIT Health offices.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify your EIT Health regional office (CLC or InnoStars)
Submit the application form with a milestone-based work plan and budget
Jury pitch/interview
Grant agreement and milestone-based payment

documents_required.doc: Business plan / commercialisation plan
Milestone and budget plan
Company registration documents

eligibility.other_note: Health, medtech, biotech or digital health start-up registered in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country. Some rounds require the company to be an EIT Health alumnus or partner-nominated.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Innovation Uptake Call
programmes.amount_note: Supports adoption and scale-up of validated health innovations into health systems. Per-project budget set in the call text.
programmes.deadline_note: Opened for 2026 alongside the Innovation Validation Call; deadlines in the call documentation.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium-based; typically requires health system or payer partners.

programmes.name_en: EIT Health Innovation Validation Call
programmes.amount_note: Grant funding to validate health innovations with users, payers and regulators. Per-project budget is set in the call text.
programmes.deadline_note: One of two EIT Health calls opened for 2026 (alongside the Innovation Uptake Call). Deadlines are published in the call documentation on the EIT Health and EIT websites.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants normally need to be, or partner with, an EIT Health partner organisation.

programmes.name_en: EIT HEI Initiative: Innovation Capacity Building for Higher Education
programmes.funder: EIT (implemented by EIT RawMaterials on behalf of the EIT Community)
programmes.amount_note: Funding for consortia of higher education institutions to build entrepreneurship and innovation capacity, including spin-out support. Published figures have been up to around EUR 1.2 million per consortium over two phases. Not a direct start-up grant, but the route through which many EU university incubators are financed.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual call for HEI consortia.
programmes.reopen_note: Calls have been issued in successive years; check eit-hei.eu for the next round.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are higher education institutions in consortia (min. 3 HEIs from 3 countries plus non-HEI partners). Start-ups benefit indirectly via university support services.

programmes.name_en: EIT InnoEnergy Highway
programmes.amount_note: EIT InnoEnergy invests in sustainable-energy start-ups and takes an equity stake, alongside a business acceleration package (market access, industrial partners, recruitment). Ticket sizes are negotiated per company and are not published as a fixed figure; InnoEnergy typically invests at seed and Series A.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling application through the InnoEnergy Highway intake form; assessment runs continuously with periodic investment committees.

eligibility.other_note: Sustainable energy, storage, e-mobility, green hydrogen and raw-materials-for-energy start-ups. European presence expected.

programmes.name_en: EIT InnoEnergy startup investment and support
programmes.amount_note: Combination of equity investment and in-kind business acceleration. Ticket sizes are negotiated case by case and are not published.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications accepted on a rolling basis through the InnoEnergy startup application form.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the online startup application form describing the technology, team and market
Screening and due diligence by an InnoEnergy thematic team
Investment committee decision; support delivered as capital plus access to the InnoEnergy industrial network

eligibility.other_note: Focus areas include energy storage, transport and mobility, decarbonising industry, smart grids and renewable energy. Created in 2010 by the European Institute of Innovation and Technology; network of over 1,400 partners.

programmes.source_snippet: InnoEnergy fast-tracks your startup path to success and industrialisation making your business case happen bigger, sooner, and safer.

programmes.name_en: EIT Jumpstarter (cross-KIC pre-accelerator)
programmes.funder: EIT (cross-KIC programme led by EIT Health with EIT Food, EIT Manufacturing, EIT RawMaterials, EIT Urban Mobility, EIT InnoEnergy)
programmes.amount_note: Free pre-accelerator for pre-company teams and very early start-ups, focused on Central, Eastern and Southern Europe. Winners in each vertical receive a cash prize (historically EUR 10,000 for the vertical winner). No equity taken.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual programme; applications have typically opened in spring and closed around May-June, with the final in November.
programmes.reopen_note: EIT Jumpstarter has run annually since 2018; the next call is published on eitjumpstarter.eu in spring.

eligibility.other_note: Open to individuals and teams with an idea (no company required), with a strong focus on EIT RIS countries in Central, Eastern and Southern Europe.

programmes.name_en: EIT Manufacturing BoostUp! competition
programmes.amount_note: Pan-European competition with regional heats and a European final, in Create / Grow / Expand categories. Winners receive cash prizes (historically in the EUR 10,000-50,000 range per category) plus access to EIT Manufacturing's industrial network. Equity-free.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual competition; regional heats usually run in spring/summer with the European final in autumn.
programmes.reopen_note: BoostUp! has run every year since 2020; regional calls are published on eitmanufacturing.eu and by the regional CLCs (Central, East, North, South, West).

eligibility.other_note: Start-ups, scale-ups and innovators with manufacturing-related solutions from EIT Manufacturing's regional coverage.

programmes.name_en: EIT RawMaterials Booster Call
programmes.amount_note: Booster funding for raw-materials start-ups and SMEs. The Booster call has offered non-dilutive funding in staged tickets, with published maxima up to around EUR 300,000 for the largest track; smaller Ideation/Prototyping tracks award less. Confirm the ticket size in the live call text.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual Booster call with a single deadline, historically in Q1-Q2.
programmes.reopen_note: The Booster call has been repeated annually; EIT RawMaterials announces the next edition on eitrawmaterials.eu.

eligibility.other_note: Start-ups/SMEs working along the raw materials value chain (exploration, mining, processing, substitution, recycling, circular economy) registered in an EU/associated country.

programmes.name_en: EIT Urban Mobility Accelerator
programmes.amount_note: Equity-free accelerator connecting mobility start-ups with European cities for pilots. Some tracks award grant funding for city pilot deployments; amounts vary by track and are stated in each call.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual cohorts plus separate city-challenge calls; application windows are announced per programme.
programmes.reopen_note: EIT Urban Mobility publishes an annual Business Creation call portfolio; watch eiturbanmobility.eu/for-business.

eligibility.other_note: Urban mobility and logistics start-ups able to run a pilot with a European city partner.

programmes.name_en: EIT Water (Knowledge and Innovation Community)
programmes.funder: EIT Water / European Institute of Innovation and Technology
programmes.amount_note: Newest EIT Innovation Community, designated in 2025 to address water resilience. Its start-up-facing instruments (acceleration, incubation, business creation calls) are being rolled out; funding amounts are not yet published as standing figures.
programmes.deadline_note: Business creation calls are expected to follow the standard EIT pattern of annual calls once the community's first business plan is in force.
programmes.reopen_note: EIT Water was formally launched in November 2025; its first start-up calls are expected as the community stands up its co-location centres. Watch eit.europa.eu and the EIT Water community site.

eligibility.other_note: Water resilience, water treatment, water reuse and water-in-industry innovators in the EU and Horizon Europe associated countries.

programmes.source_snippet: EIT Water Launched: New Innovation Community to Tackle Europe's Water Challenges

programmes.name_en: Enterprise Europe Network (EEN)
programmes.funder: European Commission (EISMEA), Single Market Programme, with national co-funding
programmes.amount_note: Free of charge to the SME. Services include international partner search and brokerage, the partnering opportunities database, EU funding advice, IP and regulatory guidance, and the Enhancing SME Innovation Management Capacity service (a multi-day free consultancy engagement). No cash is paid to the company.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous. Contact your local EEN partner organisation (usually a chamber of commerce, regional development agency or technology centre) at any time.

procedure_steps.detail: Find your local EEN contact point using the network search on een.ec.europa.eu
Request an initial diagnostic meeting
Agree an action plan (partner search, funding advice, innovation management support)
Publish or search partnering profiles in the EEN database

eligibility.other_note: SMEs established in an EEN participating country (all EU Member States plus many third countries). Free at the point of use.

programmes.name_local: ERA-NET Cofund and co-funded European Partnerships
programmes.name_en: ERA-NET Cofund / co-funded European Partnership transnational calls
programmes.funder: Consortia of national research funding agencies, co-funded by the European Commission under Horizon Europe
programmes.amount_note: Transnational joint calls where each partner is paid by its own national agency at national rates (SME rates commonly 50-70%). Typical project budgets are EUR 0.5-2 million across the consortium. Examples of active partnership families: Driving Urban Transitions, Water4All, Biodiversa+, CETPartnership, Chemicals Risk Assessment, Transforming Health and Care Systems.
programmes.deadline_note: Each partnership issues its own annual or biennial joint call, most with a two-stage pre-proposal/full-proposal structure. Deadlines are scattered across the year; ERA-LEARN maintains the consolidated calendar.

procedure_steps.detail: Find an open joint call on ERA-LEARN or the partnership website
Check your own country's national eligibility annex and funding rate - these differ sharply between agencies
Form a transnational consortium meeting the call's minimum country requirement
Submit the joint pre-proposal, then the full proposal if invited
National funding decisions and national grant agreements

eligibility.other_note: Consortium of partners from at least two or three participating countries. National annexes decide whether companies (as opposed to research organisations) are fundable in your country - in some agencies SMEs are excluded from specific calls.

programmes.name_en: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs (EYE)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly financial assistance to new entrepreneurs to cover travel and subsistence during a 1-6 month stay with an experienced entrepreneur abroad. The monthly rate is set per host country and published in the country table; it is a contribution to costs, not a business grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous open application through the EYE online tool; matching happens on a rolling basis via local intermediary organisations.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs online platform
Get validated by a local intermediary organisation
Search for and agree a match with a host entrepreneur abroad
Sign the commitment to quality and the financial agreement
Complete the exchange and reporting

eligibility.other_note: New entrepreneurs must either have a firm intention to start a business or have started one within the last three years, and be permanently resident in a participating country. Hosts must run an SME with more than three years' experience.

programmes.name_en: ESA Space Solutions Kick-Start activities
programmes.funder: European Space Agency, Directorate of Commercialisation, Industry and Procurement
programmes.amount_note: Kick-Start activities fund a short feasibility study (typically six months) with a ceiling commonly set at EUR 75,000 per activity, co-funded by ESA at up to 80% (the balance is the company's own contribution). Successful Kick-Starts can progress to a Demonstration Project worth substantially more.
programmes.deadline_note: ESA publishes thematic Kick-Start calls several times a year, each with a fixed deadline. Themes rotate (e.g. health, agriculture, energy, maritime, defence and security).

procedure_steps.detail: Check that your ESA Member State has subscribed to the relevant programme line and confirm national authorisation
Register on ESA STAR and obtain a bidder code
Respond to an open Kick-Start theme with the ESA proposal template
Evaluation by ESA and the national delegation
Contract signature and six-month activity

documents_required.doc: ESA STAR registration and bidder code
Technical and management proposal
Cost breakdown / financial proposal
Letter of authorisation from the national delegation

eligibility.other_note: Company must be registered in an ESA Member State that has subscribed to the relevant programme element. The service must use space assets (satcom, satnav, Earth observation, human spaceflight technology) in a commercially viable way.

programmes.name_en: ESA BIC (European Space Agency Business Incubation Centres)
programmes.funder: European Space Agency with national and regional co-funding partners
programmes.amount_note: Two-year incubation. The headline package usually combines an equity-free incentive for technical development (commonly around EUR 50,000 per company, but set by each national BIC and its co-funders), free or subsidised office space, technical support hours from ESA experts and business coaching. Amounts and co-funding requirements differ materially between the 25+ ESA BICs across Europe, so check the specific BIC's call.
programmes.deadline_note: Each ESA BIC runs its own call, most with two to four cut-offs per year (commonly spring and autumn). There is almost always an open ESA BIC call somewhere in Europe.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose the ESA BIC in the country/region where you will be based
Check that your product has a genuine space link (space technology used on Earth, or a downstream service using satellite data/navigation/communications)
Submit the BIC application form and business plan by the local cut-off
Technical and business review, then jury interview
Incubation agreement and start of the two-year programme

documents_required.doc: Business plan
Description of the space technology link
Financial projections
Company registration or intent to incorporate

eligibility.other_note: Start-ups typically less than five years old with a space-related product, either space upstream or space-enabled downstream. Company must be (or become) established in the BIC's country. Many BICs restrict entry to companies not previously incubated elsewhere.

programmes.name_en: ESA Business Incubation Centre network
programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA) with national and regional co-funders
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50,000 equity-free funding for product and IP development, plus up to two years of incubation, technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal and IPR advice and fundraising support.
programmes.deadline_note: Each ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. 36 centres across 23 European countries with over 100 locations; more than 2,000 startups supported.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the local ESA BIC to discuss whether the business idea fits
Submit the completed application documents before the announced local deadline
Applications are reviewed by a Tender Opening Board
Shortlisted applicants present to a Tender Evaluation Board
On approval, register a company before signing the incubation contract

documents_required.doc: Business plan
Technical description of the space link
Financial plan
Founder CVs

eligibility.other_note: Business must either use space-based systems (satellite navigation, Earth observation, satellite communication), use space technologies in a non-space domain, or develop innovative products and services for the space sector. Company must be registered in the host country before contract signature; companies must normally be younger than five years.

programmes.source_snippet: €50k equity free funding for product and IP development

programmes.name_en: ESA Space Solutions Kick-start Activity
programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA Space Solutions / Business Applications)
programmes.amount_note: Kick-start Activities fund a short feasibility study of a commercial service using space assets, historically up to EUR 75,000 per company at up to 80% funding. Successful Kick-starts can progress to a larger Demonstration Project.
programmes.deadline_note: ESA publishes themed Kick-start calls several times a year, each with its own closing date, plus a continuously open 'Open Call' for Demonstration Projects.

eligibility.other_note: Applicant must be registered in an ESA Member State that subscribes to the Business Applications programme, and the national delegation must endorse the activity.

programmes.name_en: ESA Space Solutions Demonstration Projects
programmes.funder: European Space Agency, Directorate of Commercialisation, Industry and Procurement
programmes.amount_note: Larger follow-on to Kick-Start: ESA funds a pre-operational demonstration of a space-enabled service with real users. Co-funding is typically 50% ESA / 50% company or partner contribution (higher ESA share possible for SMEs in some programme lines). Project values commonly run from several hundred thousand to a few million euro.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuously open for proposals in most participating Member States, subject to national budget availability. ESA recommends contacting your national ESA Space Solutions ambassador before submitting.

eligibility.other_note: Registered in a participating ESA Member State with national delegation authorisation. Requires committed pilot users and a credible route to commercial operation.

programmes.name_en: ESA InCubed (Investing in Industrial Innovation, Earth observation)
programmes.funder: European Space Agency Phi-lab / Earth Observation Programmes
programmes.amount_note: Co-funds the development of commercial Earth observation products and services. ESA typically covers up to 50-80% of project cost depending on the company's size and the maturity of the product, with the applicant funding the rest. Project sizes are negotiated case by case and have ranged widely.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuously open: InCubed accepts ideas at any time through its online idea submission, followed by a structured proposal phase.

eligibility.other_note: Company registered in an ESA Member State participating in the InCubed programme. Requires a commercial Earth observation product with a clear business case and co-investment.

programmes.name_en: ESA Spark Funding (technology transfer / Technology Broker Network)
programmes.funder: European Space Agency Technology Transfer Programme, delivered by national Technology Brokers
programmes.amount_note: Small, fast, equity-free grants for non-space companies to adapt and apply a space technology to a terrestrial market. Amounts are set by each national Technology Broker and typically sit in the low tens of thousands of euro per project, often with a co-funding requirement.
programmes.deadline_note: Run by national ESA Technology Brokers with their own periodic calls; availability depends on whether your country funds a Spark Funding line.

eligibility.other_note: Company registered in an ESA Member State that operates a Spark Funding scheme. The project must transfer an existing space technology into a non-space application.

programmes.name_en: EU Prize for Women Innovators
programmes.amount_note: Cash prizes awarded in two categories (Women Innovators and Rising Innovators). Prize values are set each edition in the EIC Work Programme; historically EUR 100,000 for first place in the main category and EUR 50,000 for Rising Innovators.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual contest; applications have typically opened in spring/summer and closed in late summer, with the award ceremony at the EIC Summit.
programmes.reopen_note: Runs every year; the next edition is announced on the EIC website, usually with a summer deadline.

eligibility.other_note: Applicant must be a woman who founded or co-founded an innovative company registered in the EU or a Horizon Europe associated country at least two years before the deadline. Rising Innovators category is for women aged 35 or under.

programmes.name_en: EU Defence Innovation Scheme under the European Defence Fund
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG DEFIS), European Defence Fund
programmes.amount_note: EUDIS bundles start-up-facing measures inside the European Defence Fund: dedicated calls for SMEs and non-traditional defence suppliers, a business accelerator with equity-free support, hackathons, matchmaking and an equity facility delivered via the EIF. Grant amounts are set per call; EDF projects range from about EUR 1 million to tens of millions.
programmes.deadline_note: EDF publishes one main call cycle per year, typically opening in Q2 with deadlines in autumn. EUDIS accelerator and hackathon activities have their own windows.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants must be established in the EU or Norway and not be subject to control by a non-associated third country, unless a guarantee is approved. Dual-use and defence-relevant technologies only.

programmes.name_en: EUIPO SME Fund 2026, craft and industrial geographical indications voucher
programmes.amount_note: Reimbursement of up to 50% of eligible costs related to craft and industrial geographical indication (CIGI) applications, up to a maximum of EUR 2,000 per beneficiary.
programmes.deadline_note: Available within the 2 February to 4 December 2026 SME Fund window.

procedure_steps.detail: Check you meet the EU SME definition and that the voucher you need still has budget
Create an EUIPO account and apply on the SME Fund 2026 page (first come, first served)
Receive the voucher decision, then file the IP application and pay the office fee yourself
Activate the voucher and submit a reimbursement request within the voucher validity period
EUIPO pays the reimbursement to the bank account provided

documents_required.doc: VAT or tax identification number certificate
Bank statement showing company name, IBAN and BIC
Declaration of honour if an external representative applies on your behalf

eligibility.other_note: For producer groups and SMEs registering craft or industrial geographical indications under the EU CIGI regulation.

programmes.source_snippet: reimbursement for up to 50% of eligible costs related to craft and industrial geographical indication (CIGI) applications up to a maximum of EUR 2 000 per beneficiary

programmes.name_en: EUIPO SME Fund 2026, Voucher 1: IP Scan and IP Scan Enforcement
programmes.funder: European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) with the European Commission
programmes.amount_note: 90% reimbursement of the cost of an IP Scan (a structured IP audit by an approved national expert), maximum EUR 1,620. The same ceiling applies to IP Scan Enforcement. Not available in every Member State - only where the national IP office offers the service.
programmes.deadline_note: SME Fund 2026 runs 2 February to 4 December 2026, first come first served. Voucher 1 is unavailable for new applications because its funds are exhausted.
programmes.reopen_note: The SME Fund has been re-launched every year since 2021 with a fresh budget, usually opening in January or February. Voucher 1 budget is normally consumed early in the year, so apply in the first weeks of the window.

programmes.deadline_note: SME Fund 2026 window is 2 February to 4 December 2026. Voucher 2 is currently unavailable: its funds are exhausted.
programmes.reopen_note: Re-launched annually with a new budget, historically opening in January/February. Voucher 2 is the most heavily used and is exhausted fastest - apply in the opening weeks.

programmes.amount_note: 75% of national patent fees up to EUR 1,000, and 75% of European patent filing and search fees plus 50% of European patent legal costs (legal costs capped at EUR 1,500), within an overall ceiling of EUR 2,500 per beneficiary.

programmes.name_en: Innowwide (Eureka market feasibility vouchers)
programmes.amount_note: Lump-sum grant of EUR 60,000 per Viability Assessment Project, to fund a market feasibility study with a partner in a third country outside Europe. 100% funded, equity-free.
programmes.deadline_note: Run as periodic calls with fixed cut-offs; several rounds have been held.
programmes.reopen_note: Innowwide has run in successive funded phases; continuation depends on the current EU support contract. Check innowwide.eu for an open call before relying on it.

eligibility.other_note: European SME (EU or Horizon Europe associated country) partnering with a local counterpart in an emerging or developing market.

programmes.name_en: Eureka Network Projects (bilateral and multilateral calls)
programmes.amount_note: Bottom-up international R&D collaboration. Each partner is funded by its own national body at national rates; there is no central Eureka budget. Calls are bilateral (e.g. Germany-Israel, Spain-Canada) or multilateral (Globalstars).
programmes.deadline_note: Network Projects are open on a rolling basis in some countries and via fixed bilateral/Globalstars calls in others. Check the calls page for the currently open windows.

eligibility.other_note: At least two partners from two different Eureka countries. No thematic restriction; must be civil application.

programmes.name_en: Eurostars (Eureka / Horizon Europe co-funded partnership)
programmes.funder: Eureka Association with the European Union (Innovative SMEs partnership)
programmes.amount_note: Funding is paid by each participating country's national funding body at its own rate, not centrally. Typical SME rates range from 50% to 70% of eligible project costs (e.g. Austria up to 60%, Flanders 60-70%, Canada up to 50% capped at CAD 500,000). Some countries have no budget for a given cut-off.
programmes.deadline_note: Two cut-offs per year, typically March and September. Call 10 closed in March 2026. Call 11 opened 9 July 2026 and closes 10 September 2026, 14:00 CEST.

procedure_steps.detail: Check your country's national eligibility rules and available budget for the cut-off
Build a consortium: at least two independent entities from at least two Eurostars countries, led by an innovative SME
Ensure SMEs from Eurostars countries carry 50% or more of total project cost
Submit the joint application in the Eureka portal before the cut-off
Central international evaluation and ranking; national funding decisions follow
Sign national grant agreements with each partner's own funding body

documents_required.doc: Joint project application form
Work package and cost breakdown per partner
SME declaration for the lead partner
National annexes required by each partner's funding body

eligibility.other_note: Consortium led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country. Projects must be exclusively civil applications and last 36 months or less. Eurostars countries include EU Member States plus associated and partner countries (e.g. UK, Switzerland, Turkey, Israel, South Korea, Canada, Singapore, South Africa).

programmes.source_snippet: Opening: 9 July 2026 ... Deadline: 10 September 2026, 2:00 PM CEST

programmes.name_en: Horizon Europe Pillar II Cluster 1: Health
programmes.amount_note: Collaborative R&I actions. Budgets are set per topic and typically run EUR 2-20 million per project. Research and Innovation Actions (RIA) fund 100% of eligible costs; Innovation Actions (IA) fund 70% for for-profit entities and 100% for non-profits. SMEs normally participate as consortium partners rather than as sole applicants.
programmes.deadline_note: Topics are published in the biennial Horizon Europe Work Programme (currently 2026-2027) with one or two deadlines per topic per year, most commonly in February/March and September/October.

procedure_steps.detail: Search the topic on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
Assemble a consortium meeting the minimum condition (usually 3 independent legal entities from 3 different EU/associated countries)
Register all partners for a PIC number
Draft Part B of the proposal against the topic's expected outcomes
Submit via the Funding & Tenders Portal before the deadline
Evaluation by independent experts; grant agreement preparation for successful proposals

documents_required.doc: Proposal Part A (administrative forms)
Proposal Part B (technical description, max page limit per call)
Participant Identification Code (PIC) for every partner
Ethics self-assessment
Financial capacity documents
documents_required.note: Required for coordinators requesting large amounts

eligibility.other_note: Most topics require a consortium of at least three independent legal entities from three different EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries. SMEs and start-ups are eligible partners and often specifically encouraged in the topic text.

programmes.name_en: European Hydrogen Bank - competitive auction (Innovation Fund)
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG CLIMA / CINEA), financed by EU ETS revenues
programmes.amount_note: Fixed premium paid per kilogram of renewable hydrogen produced, awarded by competitive auction with a bid ceiling set in each auction's terms. Support is paid over ten years of operation against verified production, not as an upfront capital grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Auctions have been run roughly annually, each with a fixed bid submission window of a few weeks.
programmes.reopen_note: The Commission has committed to repeated Hydrogen Bank auction rounds financed from the Innovation Fund; subsequent auctions are announced by CINEA with their own terms and bid ceiling.

eligibility.other_note: Renewable hydrogen production projects in the EEA meeting the RFNBO definition, with a final investment decision achievable within the auction timetable.

programmes.name_en: Interregional Innovation Investments Instrument (I3)
programmes.funder: European Commission (EISMEA), European Regional Development Fund
programmes.amount_note: Supports interregional investment portfolios in shared smart-specialisation priorities. Strand 1 (investment-ready portfolios) and Strand 2 (less developed regions) grants have run in the EUR 1-10 million range per project, with co-funding rates of 50-70%. Many I3 projects re-grant to SMEs through open cascade calls.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual calls under the I3 work programme, typically opening in spring with autumn deadlines.
programmes.reopen_note: I3 runs annual calls for the 2021-2027 period; watch EISMEA for the next strand 1 and strand 2 windows.

eligibility.other_note: Consortia of at least three legal entities from three countries, including regions with matching smart-specialisation priorities. SMEs are eligible partners and cascade beneficiaries.

programmes.deadline_note: One or two calls per year published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, usually opening in Q1 or Q2 with deadlines a few months later.
programmes.reopen_note: Each Joint Undertaking publishes an annual work programme setting the next call dates; check the JU website for the current calendar.

eligibility.other_note: Consortium requirements as in Horizon Europe. SMEs and start-ups participate as consortium partners; some JUs give SMEs a higher funding rate or reserved budget. Membership of the JU's private association is not required to apply but is common among coordinators.

programmes.name_en: EU Innovation Fund - Battery Manufacturing Call
programmes.amount_note: Dedicated battery cell manufacturing call run within the IF24 package (total IF24 budget EUR 4.6 billion across two regular calls and one auction). No dedicated battery call was repeated in IF25.
programmes.deadline_note: Launched with the IF24 package on 3 December 2024; the dedicated battery call was not repeated in the IF25 package launched 4 December 2025.
programmes.reopen_note: Not repeated in IF25. Battery manufacturing remains eligible under the general Net-Zero Technologies call, which explicitly covers manufacturing of components for energy storage including electric-vehicle batteries.
programmes.source_snippet: IF24 calls launched 3 December 2024 with EUR 4.6 billion: two regular calls (IF24 NZT Call, IF24 Battery Call) and one auction.

programmes.name_en: EU Innovation Fund - general decarbonisation calls
programmes.funder: European Commission (DG CLIMA / CINEA), financed by EU ETS revenues
programmes.amount_note: Grants cover up to 60% of the relevant costs (additional capital and operating expenditure versus a conventional plant). Projects are grouped by capital expenditure size: small-scale (below EUR 20m capex), medium-scale (EUR 20-100m) and large-scale (above EUR 100m). Individual awards have ranged from a few million to over EUR 200 million.
programmes.deadline_note: One main call per year, typically opening in Q4 and closing in Q1-Q2 of the following year, with separate budget envelopes per capex band.
programmes.reopen_note: The Innovation Fund has run an annual call since 2020 and is scheduled to continue through 2030 using ETS revenues; the next call is announced by CINEA, usually opening in the last quarter of the year.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the capex band your project falls into
Register on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
Prepare the single-stage application: GHG avoidance calculation, degree of innovation, maturity, scalability and cost efficiency
Submit before the call deadline
Evaluation and, for selected projects, grant agreement with CINEA

documents_required.doc: Application form Part A and Part B
GHG emission avoidance calculation
Financial model and business plan
Evidence of permits and site control

eligibility.other_note: Projects must be located in an EU Member State (or Norway/Iceland). Applicants can be any legal entity including SMEs and start-ups, but projects must be first-of-a-kind commercial-scale demonstrations of innovative low-carbon technology.

programmes.name_local: Innovation Fund Industrial Heat Auction (IF25/IF26 Heat Auction)
programmes.name_en: EU Innovation Fund - Industrial Process Heat Auction
programmes.amount_note: IF25 Heat Auction budget up to EUR 1 billion; a second round in 2026 also carries a EUR 1 billion budget. Support is auctioned to the most cost-effective CO2 abatement bids.
programmes.deadline_note: IF25 Heat Auction bids closed 19 February 2026. A second (IF26) Heat Auction round is planned for 2026 with a EUR 1 billion budget; draft terms went to public consultation with a stakeholder workshop on 7 July 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Second round of the IF Heat Auction confirmed for 2026 with a budget of EUR 1 billion.

eligibility.other_note: Open to all industrial sectors and project sizes; technologies include heat pumps, electric boilers, resistance and induction heating, solar thermal and geothermal, and hybrids.

programmes.source_snippet: A second round of the IF Heat Auction will be held in 2026 with a budget of EUR 1 billion.

programmes.name_local: European Hydrogen Bank Auction (IF25 Hydrogen Auction)
programmes.name_en: EU Innovation Fund - European Hydrogen Bank Auction
programmes.amount_note: Third auction budget EUR 1.3 billion. Support is a fixed premium per kilogram of hydrogen produced, paid for up to 10 years on verified and certified production.
programmes.deadline_note: Bids for the IF25 Hydrogen Auction closed 19 February 2026 17:00 CET. Grant agreements expected within nine months of closure.
programmes.reopen_note: The Commission ran a public consultation on the draft terms and conditions of the IF26 Hydrogen Auction until 24 August 2026, indicating a further auction round.

eligibility.other_note: RFNBO renewable hydrogen or electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen producers; IF25 added a topic for producers with maritime or aviation offtakers. Member States may top up via Auctions-as-a-Service (Spain dedicated EUR 415 million to hydrogen under IF25).

programmes.source_snippet: A second round of the IF Heat Auction will be held in 2026 with a budget of EUR 1 billion.

programmes.name_en: EU Innovation Fund - Net-Zero Technologies Call
programmes.amount_note: IF25 NZT call budget EUR 2.9 billion. Grants cover up to 60% of relevant costs. Project sizes range from small-scale/pilot to large-scale; no single fixed per-project cap published for all categories.
programmes.deadline_note: IF25 NZT call opened 4 December 2025 and closed 23 April 2026 17:00 CET. Calls typically open at the end of the year.
programmes.reopen_note: Innovation Fund calls have opened each year in late November/December (IF23 on 23 Nov 2023, IF24 on 3 Dec 2024, IF25 on 4 Dec 2025). An IF26 cycle is expected on the same rhythm; the Commission ran a public consultation on IF26 auction terms in mid-2026.

Prepare Part A (administrative) and Part B (technical) of the application, including the GHG avoidance calculation

programmes.source_snippet: There are currently no open Innovation Fund calls. Calls typically open at the end of the year.

programmes.amount_note: Dedicated budget envelope for projects with total capital expenditure below EUR 20 million. Grants cover up to 60% of relevant costs. Simplified application compared to the large-scale band, which makes this the realistic Innovation Fund route for scale-ups.
programmes.deadline_note: Part of the annual Innovation Fund call; the small-scale envelope has its own budget line and simplified template.
programmes.reopen_note: Recurs with each annual Innovation Fund call. In recent work programmes the capex bands were restructured, so confirm the current thresholds in the live call text.

eligibility.other_note: Total capital expenditure below the published small-scale threshold. Located in an EU Member State, Norway or Iceland.

programmes.amount_note: Large collaborative projects, typically EUR 10-30 million total, with EU cash contribution matched by in-kind contributions from industry partners. SMEs and startups receive EU cash funding as consortium beneficiaries.

programmes.deadline_note: Calls for interregional cooperation projects open roughly once a year for a fixed window of about two months.
programmes.reopen_note: Interreg Europe has run a call in most years of the 2021-2027 period; the next call is announced on interregeurope.eu.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are public authorities, agencies and non-profit bodies from EU Member States plus Norway and Switzerland. SMEs benefit indirectly through improved regional instruments.

programmes.name_en: Interreg A/B programmes running SME innovation and cascade schemes

programmes.amount_note: Many Interreg B (transnational) and Interreg A (cross-border) programmes fund projects that then run vouchers or small grants for SMEs in the programme area, typically EUR 5,000-50,000 per company. Project co-funding is usually 65-80% ERDF. Terms and eligible territory vary programme by programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Each Interreg programme runs its own call calendar; across the ~80 programmes there is almost always an open call somewhere. Check interreg.eu and your regional programme's site.

eligibility.other_note: The company must be located in the programme's eligible territory. Direct applicants for project funding are usually consortia including public bodies; SMEs typically apply to a project's own voucher call.

programmes.name_en: InvestEU SME Window (guarantees and equity via financial intermediaries)
programmes.funder: European Commission with the European Investment Bank Group (EIB, EIF) and other implementing partners
programmes.amount_note: Not a grant and not applied for directly. InvestEU provides an EU budget guarantee that lets banks, guarantee institutions, leasing companies, venture debt providers and VC funds lend to or invest in SMEs on better terms. Founders access it by borrowing from an accredited local intermediary, which discloses InvestEU backing in the loan documentation.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous. Financial intermediaries are selected via EIF calls for expression of interest; SMEs apply to the intermediary at any time.

procedure_steps.detail: Use the EIF or InvestEU 'find a financial intermediary' search for your country
Apply for financing directly to that bank, guarantee body or fund
The intermediary applies the InvestEU-backed terms (reduced collateral, longer tenor or lower rate) as part of its normal credit process

eligibility.other_note: SME or small mid-cap established in an EU Member State. Final eligibility and pricing are set by the intermediary.

eligibility.other_note: 'HaDEA implements the EU4Health programme by managing calls for proposals and tenders from 2021 to 2027', aimed at 'the resilience of European healthcare systems'.
